history.period: Stepwell said to be 15th century (single reviewer claim, unverified)
history.summary: Bhadrakali Mata shrine associated with the old Bhadrakali Vav (stepwell) in the middle of Umreth town (Wada Bazar, Lakiya Pore), Anand district. A shrine to Devi Bhadrakali stands on the stepwell's first storey and its aarti is locally famous (Google reviews). The vav is described as a 15th-century, L-shaped seven-storey stepwell (single-reviewer claim, unverified); no authoritative documented history found. CSV town 'Anand' corrected to Umreth (~25 km from Anand); no Bhadrakali Mata temple is documented in Anand city itself, and the famous regional Bhadrakali Mataji shrine at Bhadra Fort, Ahmedabad (~55 km away) is a different site. Identity as the CSV row's referent is probable but not certain.

name: Bhadrakali Mata Temple (Bhadrakali Vav, Umreth)
town_description: Umreth is a town in Anand district, Gujarat, about 25 km from Anand on the Anand-Godhra road and rail route. It is known for its old stepwells, including the Bhadrakali Vav.

travel.road: In Umreth town centre (Wada Bazar, Lakiya Pore), on GJ SH 12
